note: What a companion's three stat classes are, and where they do NOT come from. Read by the player from the in-game Companion UI and paired with the exact save-file record of the same pet. The save's own PetBattlerCoreStatClassOverrides is inert and must never be shown as the class.
method: Pets read from BaseContext.PlayerStateData.Pets of save2.hg (slot index kept, it is a fixed 30-entry array).
The player read Combat Effectiveness / Agility / Health, and sometimes Overall, from the Companion UI.
Two same-species clone pairs in this save isolate one variable each; see 'experiments'.
To add a later reading after training a pet, append to that pet's 'readings' array - do not overwrite.
conclusions: PetBattlerCoreStatClassOverrides is [C, C, C] with PetBattlerUseCoreStatClassOverrides false for every pet in the save, including brand-new ones, while the UI shows anything from C to S. It is an override slot the game ignores, not the pet's class.

Training does not change the class. Proven on the Grunt clone pair (slots 3 and 6): identical CreatureSeed, SpeciesSeed, GenusSeed, BoneScaleSeed, Descriptors and Scale; 8/10/10 treats and 44 victories versus 1/0/2 treats and 15 victories; both read A / A / S.
Size does not change the class. Proven on the Spider clone pair (slots 4 and 9): identical seeds and descriptors, Scale 2.181 versus 3.681 (69 percent bigger); both read B / A / A.
The class is therefore intrinsic and fixed at hatch - a function of the creature seeds, which the two clone pairs reading identically also demonstrates directly.

The derivation is not in the game's data tables: gccreatureglobals.mbin holds no stat, class, tier or rank strings, and the only petbattler tables are petbattlermovestable.mbin and petbattlermovesetstable.mbin (moves, not stats). It is computed in engine code.

Traits are not the stats. Using abs(trait) with a 0.50 cut fitted Callista's A/A/B exactly, then failed on all four pets it was used to predict (Mantissa predicted A/B/C, read B/A/A; three C/A/C predictions all wrong). Traits and the class are probably both seed-derived, hence correlated, not causal.

A search of every nibble, byte and 16-bit word of all six seeds for a field monotone with the observed letters found nothing for Combat or Agility, and only overlapping bits of SpeciesSeed for Health - 8 samples against about 144 candidate fields, so treated as coincidence, not a finding.

PetBattlerTreatsEaten index 2 is Combat Effectiveness, measured: the player spent 8 treats on Combat and all 8 appeared at index 2 (2 -> 10), with indices 0 and 1 unchanged. The plugin's pets.STAT_NAMES claims index 2 is Agility and is therefore WRONG about at least that index; indices 0 and 1 are still unidentified. Note this is measured for PetBattlerTreatsEaten only - whether PetBattlerCoreStatClassOverrides shares the same order is untested, and cannot be tested while every pet reads [C, C, C].
A stat caps at 10 treats eaten: Plati's Combat stopped at exactly 10 with a treat still available, which also explains Little Cute Monster's [8, 10, 10].

Training confirmed a second time, now as a before/after on one pet rather than across clones: Plati went from 2 to 10 treats on Combat Effectiveness and still reads A / A / S with Overall S. Treats do not move the class letters.

PetBattlerTreatsEaten is ordered (Health, Agility, Combat Effectiveness) - the reverse of the UI's display order. pets.STAT_NAMES = (Combat Effectiveness, Health, Agility) is wrong in all three positions.

The class letter and the trained number are independent quantities. Unzy reads Health C at a maxed 10/10 and Agility B at 1/10: a maxed stat in a low tier still shows C, an untouched stat in a better tier still shows B. The letter is the stat's unchangeable tier, fixed at hatch by the seeds, and the x/10 is treats invested. Per the player, the tier scales how much each treat is worth in that category - see what_a_tier_does - so it is a rate of return, not a cap: every stat takes 10 treats whatever its tier.
Unzy read B / B / C both before and after this training, a third confirmation that treats do not move the class - now on a pet where one stat went all the way to its cap.

Gene modification (the Morphogenetics interface) changes Aggressiveness, Helpfulness, Size and the like - stated by the player, who performed the edits - i.e. it writes Traits and Scale, NOT the battle stats and NOT the creature seeds. This reframes both clone pairs: they are gene-edited relatives, not coincidences. Plati is a gene-modified descendant of Little Cute Monster, and the two Spiders differ by a deliberate size edit (Scale 2.181 -> 3.681). So size was not merely uncorrelated with the class - it was directly altered on one creature and the class letters did not move. Traits and Scale are player-editable; the class is not.

The x/10 numbers the Companion UI shows ARE PetBattlerTreatsEaten, not a derived stat. Confirmed on two pets, six independent values, with no mismatch: Unzy stores [10, 1, 8] and reads Combat 8/10, Agility 1/10, Health 10/10; Mantissa stores [4, 0, 6] and reads Combat 6/10, Agility 0/10, Health 4/10 - the latter predicted before it was read. The cap of 10 is therefore the treat cap, and nothing numeric about a companion's battle stats is hidden from the save: the plugin can show these values exactly, from the save alone, with no guessing.

Overall is computed from the three letters alone, as ceil(mean), i.e. ceil(sum/3) with C=0 B=1 A=2 S=3. It fits all 11 pets and every simpler alternative (max, min, median, floor, round) is contradicted by at least one pet. So Overall carries no information beyond the three stats and is not worth storing separately.

Alia is both larger and heavier than Wolverine (1.0 m / 41.0 kg against 0.8 m / 30.3 kg) and reads Health C against Wolverine's S. That refutes 'larger creatures have higher inherent health' a second time, now against the size and weight the game itself prints rather than the raw Scale field.

The displayed size is Scale rounded to one decimal and the displayed weight is 40 * Scale rounded to one decimal, with 40 a single global constant. Confirmed on three species of very different build across a 4.9x range of Scale (Cat 0.8 m, Two-leg Antelope 1.0 m, Spider 3.7 m), the last predicted in advance as the falsifier. Both values can therefore be shown exactly, from Scale alone.

What a tier does: it is an unchangeable rate of return on treats, scaling how much stat each treat buys in that category - stated by the player, not measurable from a save. It is not a cap (every stat takes 10 treats whatever its tier) and not a stat value. The plugin therefore shows investment, not strength, and cannot rank companions by power.

The tier is a function of CreatureSeed ALONE - measured, not just stated. Tippo shares Unzy's CreatureSeed but has no CreatureSecondarySeed and different Descriptors, and reads the same B/B/C. The creature archetype does not bias tiers either: three Two-leg Antelopes on three seeds scatter across every stat.
open: The exact CreatureSeed -> tier function. Not recoverable from labelled pets; see creature_seed_search. Needs engine disassembly, and nothing in the plugin depends on it.

Overall still looks like a function of the three letters alone, scoring C=0 B=1 A=2 S=3, and is now monotone over three distinct sums: Unzy B/B/C sums 2 and reads Overall B; Mantissa, Zushetto and Callista all sum 5 and read A; Plati sums 7 and reads S. Consistent but underdetermined - the B/A boundary lies somewhere in 3..5 and the A/S boundary in 6..7, and no pet has yet read Overall C.
Whether treats raise the numeric stat within a class (plausible, and what 'training' would then mean) - the UI letters are all that has been read so far.

Scale looks like a seeded base plus a discrete step: the Spider clones differ by exactly 1.500 with an identical fractional part, and Callista's Scale is 1.4999999. The younger Spider is the bigger one, so it is not growth with age.

Whether size affects anything the player can see. It does not affect the class letters (proven by the Spider size edit) and it cannot affect the x/10 numbers either, because those ARE PetBattlerTreatsEaten - see the conclusion on that. So if size matters at all it is inside battle resolution, which neither the save nor the UI exposes, and this plugin cannot speak to it. An earlier version of this note proposed comparing the two Spiders' numbers as a size control; that was wrong twice over - the numbers are just treats, and the two Spiders do not even have equal treats (Mantissa [4,0,6], Zushetto [0,0,0]).

experiments.name: Grunt clone pair - isolates training
experiments.result: Both A / A / S. Training does not move the class.
experiments.player_note: Plati is a gene-modified descendant of Little Cute Monster. Gene editing rewrote Traits but left every seed identical, which is why the pair works as a clone control.

experiments.name: Spider clone pair - isolates size
experiments.result: Both B / A / A. Size does not move the class - and this is a deliberate gene edit of Size on an otherwise identical creature, not an accident of two similar pets, so it is a direct intervention test rather than a correlation.
experiments.player_note: The player gene-edited size here. Their impression that smaller creatures are more agile and larger ones tougher is not visible in the class letters; if it is real it must act on the numeric stats, which are a separate quantity (see the letter/number conclusion).

save_override_order: Unverified and untestable while every pet reads [C, C, C]. pets.STAT_NAMES claims Combat Effectiveness / Health / Agility, which the measured PetBattlerTreatsEaten order (Health / Agility / Combat Effectiveness) contradicts. Do not assume the two arrays share an order.

readings.note: After the player spent treats on Health only. 3 treats left the pool (7 -> 4) and all 3 landed on PetBattlerTreatsEaten index 0, which rose 7 -> 10. The player also read the numeric stats, which pin every index at once: Combat 8/10, Agility 1/10, Health 10/10 against the stored [10, 1, 8].

Shares Unzy Bunzy Bowa's CreatureSeed exactly but has no CreatureSecondarySeed (Unzy has 0x56427E9D16C14071) and different Descriptors - a cow hump and T-Rex feet against Unzy's feathers and long face. Predicted B/B/C before the reading. Overall was not read for this pet.

Numeric stats read by the player: Combat 6/10, Agility 0/10, Health 4/10 - matching the stored [4, 0, 6] exactly under the measured (Health, Agility, Combat) order. Predicted before the reading, so this is a confirmation rather than a fit.
Sum 4, which was an unobserved gap in the Overall fit with a predicted A.
The third Cat, on a third distinct CreatureSeed.
The largest companion in the save at 5.0 m / 199.0 kg.

Agility double-checked by the player as C. An earlier reading of this pet said B; the save record was byte-identical across both, so that was a misreading and has been discarded rather than kept as a conflict. The corrected S/C/A sums to 5 and gives Overall A, which is what was read.
Freshly tamed, untrained. The player also read the displayed size and weight.
Freshly tamed, untrained. The player also read the displayed size and weight.

After the player spent every remaining treat on Combat Effectiveness. 8 treats left the pool (9 -> 1) and all 8 landed on PetBattlerTreatsEaten index 2, which rose 2 -> 10 and stopped there, leaving 1 treat unspendable on that stat.

Size and weight read as the falsifier for the 40 kg per unit of Scale: a 3.7 m mantis is the most differently built creature in the save from the Cat and Two-leg Antelope the constant was derived from. Predicted 3.7 m / 147.3 kg before the reading; both exact.

save_treats_order.note: Fully determined, and it is the exact REVERSE of the order the Companion UI lists the stats in (UI: Combat Effectiveness, Agility, Health). Established by two independent single-stat spends - Plati's 8 treats into Combat landed on index 2, Unzy's 3 into Health landed on index 0 - and confirmed outright by Unzy's numeric stats matching the stored array element by element (Combat 8 = index 2, Agility 1 = index 1, Health 10 = index 0).

web_cross_check.provenance_warning: These claims come from web SEARCH RESULT SNIPPETS, not from reading the pages - the page fetches were not performed. Treat every wording here as second-hand. All of the sources are fan sites or secondary games press; none is Hello Games documentation.
web_cross_check.headline: No source was found that documents companion stat CLASSES (S/A/B/C) at all. Searches for them returned No Man's Sky SHIP classes instead. The grading of companion battle stats appears to be publicly undocumented, so there is nothing to cross-check the central finding against and no corroboration should be implied.

claims.claim: Giving a companion treats from the Companion Register increases its aggression stat.
claims.source: cyberpost.co (FAQ page surfaced in search; flagged single-source by the search itself)
claims.evidence: Two independent treat spends were diffed on the save. Plati: only PetBattlerTreatsAvailable (9->1) and PetBattlerTreatsEaten ([1,0,2]->[1,0,10]) changed. Unzy: only PetBattlerTreatsAvailable (7->4) and PetBattlerTreatsEaten ([7,1,8]->[10,1,8]) changed. Traits - which hold aggression and helpfulness - were byte-identical before and after in both cases. Treats feed the three battle stats only.

claims.claim: Larger creatures have higher inherent health.
claims.verdict: REFUTED for the class letters; UNTESTED for the numeric values
claims.evidence: The Spider pair is a deliberate gene edit of Size on an otherwise seed-identical creature (Scale 2.181 -> 3.681) and both read Health A. So size does not set the health CLASS. Whether it shifts the x/10 numbers is untested and remains an open question; both Spiders have zero treats, so they are the ready-made control.

claims.claim: Evolve creatures with Retroviral Pellets and gene edits to boost Combat Effectiveness, Agility and Health.
claims.verdict: CONFLICTS with the player's own account and with measurement, for the letters
claims.evidence: The player, who performed the gene edits, states the Morphogenetics interface changes Aggressiveness, Helpfulness and Size - Traits and Scale in the save - not the battle stats. No gene edit or treat spend observed in this save moved a class letter. The guides may be describing the numeric values, or loosely restating patch-note marketing; as written, the claim is not supported here.

Consistent with this research's finding that Traits are a separate axis from the stat class - abs(Traits) was tested as the source of the letters and falsified. Behaviour during a battle is not something the save records, so it cannot be checked this way.

claims.claim: Update 6.3 'Xeno Arena' (April 2026) added creature battles and a genetics interface.
claims.evidence: Matches the installed build and the save's PetBattler* fields. Nothing in this research depends on it.

claims.claim: Sources disagree on whether a companion can die in a battle or is only knocked out.
claims.source: two guides surfaced in search, in direct contradiction
claims.verdict: IRRELEVANT here, recorded as a warning
claims.evidence: Noted only as evidence that these secondary guides contradict each other on basic mechanics, which is why none of them is relied on above.

overall_formula.formula: Overall = ceil((combat + agility + health) / 3), scoring C=0, B=1, A=2, S=3
overall_formula.equivalently: the ceiling of the mean of the three letters
overall_formula.fits: all 20 pets with an Overall reading, of 21 labelled

alternatives_ruled_out.floor(sum/3): 9 misses: Unzy Bunzy Bowa, Little Cute Monster, Mantissa, Plati, Zushetto, Zero-Rex, Mandriliva, Milkinny, Callista
alternatives_ruled_out.round(mean): 3 misses: Little Cute Monster, Plati, Milkinny
alternatives_ruled_out.min: 11 misses: Unzy Bunzy Bowa, Hidippo, Little Cute Monster, Mantissa, Plati, Zushetto, Zero-Rex, Zero-Bug, Mandriliva, Milkinny, Callista
alternatives_ruled_out.median: 4 misses: Little Cute Monster, Plati, Zero-Rex, Zero-Bug

overall_formula.decisive_observation: Zero-Rex. A/C/C sums to 2, the same as Unzy's B/B/C, but has a different max (A vs B) and a different median (C vs B). Both read Overall B, which eliminates max and median at a stroke - no single-letter statistic can produce it.
overall_formula.caveat: Fitted over 7 distinct sums ([2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9]) rather than derived from the game's code, but it has now predicted two previously unobserved sums correctly in advance. Gaps: [0, 1, 8].
overall_formula.confirmed_predictions: Two sums have now been predicted before any pet existed at them and then read correctly: sum 9 (Wolverine S/S/S -> S) and sum 4 (Buzita S/C/B -> A). Only sums 0, 1 and 8 remain unobserved.

measured_on: Wolverine ^CAT: Scale 0.757267 -> 0.8 m, 30.3 kg (game: 0.8 m, 30.3 kg)
Alia ^TWOLEGANTELOPE: Scale 1.025970 -> 1.0 m, 41.0 kg (game: 1.0 m, 41.0 kg)
Zushetto ^SPIDER: Scale 3.681337 -> 3.7 m, 147.3 kg (game: 3.7 m, 147.3 kg) - predicted in advance, as the falsifier for the weight constant
size_and_weight.status: CONFIRMED on three species with very different builds - a Cat (0.8 m), a Two-leg Antelope (1.0 m) and a 3.7 m Spider/mantis - spanning a 4.9x range of Scale, every value exact to the printed decimal. The 40 kg per unit of Scale is a single global constant, not a per-species density: a species-dependent weight could not have survived the Spider, which was predicted before it was read precisely because it is the least cat-like body in the save.
size_and_weight.consequence_if_it_holds: The plugin could show a companion's size and weight exactly as the game does, from Scale alone - neither is currently shown anywhere.
size_and_weight.remaining_doubt: Low. All three samples are rounded to one decimal, so the constant is 40 to about three significant figures; a true value of, say, 39.99 would not show up here. Nothing in the plugin depends on more precision than the game itself prints.

what_a_tier_does.provenance: Stated by the player from their own play, NOT measured here - the save exposes neither the letter nor any resulting stat value, so this cannot be checked from a save file. Recorded separately from the measurements for that reason.
what_a_tier_does.statement: A stat's tier is unchangeable and determines how much benefit that category gets from investing in it. The tier is a rate of return on treats, not a cap on them and not a stat value in itself: every stat accepts the same 10 treats, but a higher tier converts each treat into more of that stat.
what_a_tier_does.corrects: An earlier framing in this research called the letter 'the stat's intrinsic class' and 'the ceiling's quality'. That was imprecise: the ceiling in treats is 10 for every stat regardless of tier, as Unzy's maxed 10/10 Health at tier C shows. What the tier scales is the payoff per treat.
consistent_with: Unzy reads Health C at a maxed 10/10 and Agility B at 1/10 - the letter is plainly not a function of the number, and the number is plainly not limited by the letter.
Every stat on every pet caps at 10 treats, whatever its letter (Plati's tier-A Combat stopped at 10, Unzy's tier-C Health stopped at 10).
Nothing moves a letter, which is what 'unchangeable' predicts.
what_a_tier_does.consequence: Two companions with the same treats invested are not equally strong, so the treat numbers the plugin shows are investment, not power. The tier that converts them cannot be read from the save, so the plugin cannot rank companions by strength and should not imply that it can.

tier_source.player_statement: The tier of a category is directly based on the creature seed.
tier_source.what_this_research_can_show: Isolated. Three pairs share a CreatureSeed and all three agree on every letter: Little Cute Monster/Plati A/A/S, Mantissa/Zushetto B/A/A, and Unzy/Tippo B/B/C - the last with a different secondary seed and different descriptors, which is what makes it decisive rather than merely consistent.
pairs_sharing_a_creature_seed: 0xEBE89A26D590DC7F - Little Cute Monster and Plati, both A/A/S
0x320E447D6296A867 - Unzy Bunzy Bowa (B/B/C) and the unnamed Cow in slot 1 (UNREAD)
tier_source.open_test: The unnamed Cow in slot 1 is the one discriminating pet in the save. It shares Unzy's CreatureSeed, SpeciesSeed and GenusSeed and has the same Scale, but differs in CreatureSecondarySeed (Unzy 0x56427E9D16C14071, slot 1 absent) and in its Descriptors - a visibly different animal with different body parts. If the tier is a function of CreatureSeed alone it must read exactly B/B/C like Unzy; if CreatureSecondarySeed or the descriptors enter the derivation, it can differ. Reading its three letters tests the player's statement in its strict form, and it is the only such test available without new pets.
tier_source.measured_2026_10_20: CONFIRMED that the tier is a function of CreatureSeed alone. Tippo (slot 1) shares Unzy Bunzy Bowa's CreatureSeed byte for byte while differing in CreatureSecondarySeed (Unzy 0x56427E9D16C14071, Tippo none) and in its Descriptors - a visibly different animal, cow hump and T-Rex feet against feathers and a long face - and reads B/B/C, identical to Unzy, as predicted before the reading. So neither the secondary seed nor the descriptors enter the derivation. The player's statement now has a measurement behind it, and the earlier caveat that this save could not isolate which seed is resolved.

creature_seed_search.question: Given that the tier comes from CreatureSeed, can the derivation be recovered from labelled pets?
creature_seed_search.data: 13 pets, 11 distinct CreatureSeeds. The two duplicate-seed pairs agree on all three letters.
creature_seed_search.searched: Every 2-, 3-, 4- and 8-bit field at every offset of the 64-bit seed (about 250 fields), the seed modulo 3,4,5,6,7,8,10,12,16,20,100, its popcount and popcount%4. A field counted as a hit only if no field value ever carried two different letters.
creature_seed_search.result: NEGATIVE. Nothing survives a null test.
creature_seed_search.null_test: The same search was re-run on randomly shuffled letters, 300 trials per stat, comparing how many value-collisions the best field survived. Shuffled labels did as well or better in 300/300 trials for Combat, 61/300 (20%) for Agility and 256/300 (85%) for Health. So the apparent hits - e.g. bits[31:34] looking consistent for Agility - are what this search finds in noise, not a finding. Recorded because without the null test they look convincing.
creature_seed_search.why_it_fails: A 64-bit seed almost certainly reaches the tier through a hash or seeded PRNG, as the rest of the game's procedural generation does. No contiguous bit field of the input would then map to the output, which is exactly what is observed. Recovering it needs the function, not more input/output pairs: 11 samples cannot distinguish candidate hashes, and even hundreds would not without the right functional form to fit.
creature_seed_search.do_not_retry: Do not re-run a bit-field search on a SMALL sample (tens of seeds): two such runs came back empty with a null test showing they had no power to begin with, so a third would only produce plausible-looking fields that mean nothing. With hundreds of scanner-labelled seeds the search is worth running again, and the null test must be run alongside it every time.
creature_seed_search.what_would_work: Disassembling the engine's companion-stat code, or a community datamine of it. Neither is available, and the plugin does not need it: it shows the treat numbers, which are exact, and says plainly that the tier is not in the save.
creature_seed_search.rerun_2026_10_20: Repeated on 18 distinct CreatureSeeds, up from 11. Still negative, and more clearly so: the best field survived only 1 collision for each stat, and shuffled labels matched or beat that in 372/400, 361/400 and 365/400 trials (93%, 90%, 91%). The 15 fields that looked consistent for Agility on 11 seeds collapsed to noise level once the data doubled, which is what a chance fit does and a real one does not. This closes the question: the tier comes from CreatureSeed, but the function is not recoverable from input/output pairs.

reopened_2026_10_20.why: The two earlier searches failed on 11 and 18 labelled seeds. The scanner makes labels cheap, and the save already holds 515 distinct creature seeds, so the sample size can grow by more than an order of magnitude. Both earlier runs were low-powered: a null test showed shuffled labels matching the best field 90-93% of the time, which says the searches could not have detected a real signal either, not just that none was found.
what_a_large_labelled_set_would_buy: Power. With hundreds of samples a bit field that is consistent by chance becomes vanishingly unlikely, so a hit would mean something. At 18 samples it did not, which is exactly what the null test measured.

The ability to test specific candidate functions rather than scan for structure - the game's procedural generation uses known PRNG shapes, and a candidate can be confirmed or killed outright on 500 pairs.

Distributional facts that need no inversion at all: whether the four tiers are uniform, whether the three stats are independent of each other, whether anything correlates with species or biome. The current 21 pets already hint that S is over-represented (33%), which 500 samples would settle.
reopened_2026_10_20.what_it_still_may_not_buy: If the tier comes from a hash with good mixing, no amount of input/output pairs recovers it by search - the function has to be guessed and then tested. So a large set makes the search worth running and makes a negative result meaningful, but it does not guarantee a positive one.
reopened_2026_10_20.status: OPEN again. The do_not_retry note below applies only to re-running on small samples.

archetype_bias.question: Does the CreatureID archetype (^CAT, ^TWOLEGANTELOPE ...) bias a stat's tier?
archetype_bias.answer: NO general bias. One unexplained run remains, treated as chance.
archetype_bias.evidence_against: The three Two-leg Antelopes, on three distinct CreatureSeeds, scatter completely: Buzita S/C/B, Buza B/B/S, Alia C/S/C. No stat is shared across them. An archetype that set or biased tiers could not produce that.
archetype_bias.the_run: All three Cats read Combat S - Mandriliva S/C/A, Wolverine S/S/S, Kaky S/S/S - on three distinct CreatureSeeds. Tempting, but Combat S is the single most common tier in this roster (21/63 of all tier readings are S, 33%), so three in a row is roughly a 1-in-27 coincidence, and two archetypes were examined, which roughly doubles the chance of seeing some such run. Not significant, and flatly contradicted as a general rule by the Antelopes. A fourth Cat would decide it.
archetype_bias.note: Clone pairs carry no information here: ^COW, ^GRUNT and ^SPIDER each have two pets sharing one CreatureSeed, so their agreement is the seed, not the archetype.

record_keeping.standing_instruction: The player may delete companions when slots run out, and will keep sending new pets to read. Every pet's seeds and readings are to be kept permanently for further analysis, including for pets that no longer exist in the save.
record_keeping.identity: pet_key = '<CreatureSeed>@<BirthTime>'. CreatureSeed alone is NOT unique - clones and gene-modified descendants share one (Little Cute Monster/Plati, Mantissa/Zushetto, Unzy/Tippo) - and BirthTime separates them. Names are not identities either: the player renames pets, and a name can be reused.
record_keeping.slot_is_not_an_identity: The Pets array is a fixed 30-entry list and a freed slot is reused, so a new pet can land on a deleted pet's index. The old 'slot' field is kept as 'slot_last_seen' for locating a pet in the save at the time it was read, and must never be used to match a pet across reads.
record_keeping.when_a_pet_is_gone: Set present_in_save to false and leave everything else untouched. A deleted pet's seed and tier readings stay valid evidence - the tier is a function of CreatureSeed, which does not care whether the player still owns the animal. Never delete an observation.
how_to_add_a_reading: Re-read the save and match each pet by pet_key, not by slot and not by name.
A pet already recorded gets a new entry appended to its 'readings' array, never an overwrite - that is what makes before/after training diffs possible.
A pet not recorded yet gets a new observation with its full seed set, descriptors, traits, scale and the save-side battle record, plus the player's UI reading.

Check every new reading against the standing predictions before writing it down: Overall == ceil((combat+agility+health)/3); the x/10 numbers == PetBattlerTreatsEaten in the order (Health, Agility, Combat Effectiveness); size == round(Scale,1) m; weight == round(40*Scale,1) kg; and pets sharing a CreatureSeed must share all three letters. Report any miss rather than quietly fitting.
Mark any pet no longer in the save as present_in_save false in the same pass.
what_more_pets_can_still_settle: A fourth Cat: all three so far read Combat S, which is about a 1-in-27 coincidence and is the only archetype pattern left standing (see archetype_bias).
Sums 0, 1 and 8, the three Overall values never yet observed (predicted C, B, S).

Two creatures of the SAME species - same SpeciesSeed, different CreatureSeed. Still absent from the save. Not needed for the tier source any more (Tippo settled that), but it would confirm directly that two same-species animals can hold different tiers.
NOT the CreatureSeed -> tier function: that is closed, see creature_seed_search. More pets cannot recover a hash, and two null-tested searches have already come back empty.

Taming a creature that was scanned earlier: its CreatureSeed is already in the discovery store, so its tiers can be recorded against a seed that was known before the pet existed. Of no analytical use while the function is unknown, but it is the one way a tier reading could ever be predicted rather than observed.
record_keeping.deleted_pets_and_seeds: A deleted pet keeps its CreatureSeed recoverable through its discovery record (see scanned_creatures), but nothing else. Scale, Traits, treats, victories, trust, BirthTime and the UI readings exist only here.

scanned_creatures.finding: Every creature the player has SCANNED carries its CreatureSeed in the discovery store, whether or not it was ever tamed. Measured on the real save: 3,201 discovery records, 520 of kind Animal, 519 of those with a creature seed, 515 distinct. 433 are the player's own scans, 86 another player's.
scanned_creatures.where: DiscoveryManagerData['DiscoveryData-v1'].Store.Record, kind 'Animal', field DD.VP - a vector of 4 or 5 validation seeds. VP[0] is the CreatureSeed; discoveries.parse() exposes it as row['s'] and DiscoveryBook.animal_by_seed() keys on VP[0].
scanned_creatures.proof_that_vp0_is_the_creature_seed: All 21 tamed pets join onto a discovery record on VP[0] == CreatureSeed - 21 of 21, no misses. Previously this join was relied on by pets.first_scan() without that many confirmations.
scanned_creatures.why_this_does_NOT_help_crack_the_tier: WITHDRAWN - see CORRECTION_2026_10_20. This said the scanned seeds were unlabelled and therefore useless for the search. They are labelable with the scanner. Kept visible rather than deleted so the mistake is not repeated.
scanned_creatures.why_it_matters_anyway: A deleted companion's CreatureSeed is not lost. Its discovery record stays in the save, so the seed - the one field the tier depends on - remains recoverable for any pet whose species the player ever scanned, which is all 21 so far. What the discovery record does NOT keep is the pet-only data: Scale, Traits, treats, victories, trust, BirthTime, and the player's UI readings. For those, research/pet_classes.json is the only surviving source once a pet is deleted, which is why observations are never removed from it.
scanned_creatures.if_a_wild_seed_list_is_ever_wanted: Regenerate it from the save rather than storing 497 hex strings here: parse the Animal records and subtract the tamed pets' seeds. It is derived data and would go stale as the player scans more.
scanned_creatures.CORRECTION_2026_10_20: The player can read a creature's tiers with the in-game scanner, WITHOUT taming it. The claim recorded here that those seeds are 'unlabelled' was wrong on its premise: labels are obtainable for every creature the player can reach, not only for companions. The reasoning that followed from it - that this could not revive the seed search - does not hold and is withdrawn.

scanner_labelling_protocol.purpose: Pair a scanner tier reading to the right CreatureSeed, for creatures that are never tamed.
scanner_labelling_protocol.the_problem: An Animal discovery record carries no name - 0 of the player's 433 own records have one - so a reading cannot be matched to a record by name. It does carry the scan timestamp and the seed.
scanner_labelling_protocol.the_method: Match by scan time. Scan creatures in a known order, note each one's tiers in that order, then re-read the save and take the newest Animal records by timestamp: the Nth reading pairs with the Nth new record in ascending time order.
scanner_labelling_protocol.calibrate_first: Before any bulk run, do a batch of three. If exactly three new Animal records appear, the pairing works and the method scales. If re-scanning an already-discovered creature does NOT create a record or refresh its timestamp, the count will not match and the method has to change - that is the one assumption worth testing cheaply rather than discovering after fifty readings.
scanner_labelling_protocol.record_count_is_moving: The Animal record count went from 520 to 522 between two reads minutes apart, so the player is actively scanning. Always re-read the save immediately before pairing, and never pair against a stale dump.
scanner_labelling_protocol.validate_the_tier_itself: Worth one creature's effort: scan a wild creature, note its tiers, then tame it and read its Companion tiers. If they agree, the scanner tier IS the companion tier and the whole scanned dataset is interchangeable with the pet dataset. Until that is checked, scanner readings are stored separately from companion readings rather than pooled.
scanner_labelling_protocol.storage: Scanner readings go in a separate 'scanned_readings' list keyed by CreatureSeed, not in 'observations', which is for companions with a pet_key. A creature later tamed gets a normal observation and keeps its earlier scanner reading, which then also serves as the validation above.

untameable_creatures.finding: Not every scannable creature has tiers. The player scanned a FLYING creature, which cannot be tamed as a companion and therefore shows no C/B/A/S tiers at all. Only tameable creatures can be labelled.
untameable_creatures.why_it_matters: It breaks the naive pairing rule. 'The Nth reading pairs with the Nth new Animal record' assumed one reading per new record. An untameable creature still creates a discovery record but produces no reading, so from that point on every later pairing in the batch would be shifted by one and silently wrong - the worst kind of error here, because the seeds would still look plausible.
untameable_creatures.protocol_fix: Report EVERY scan in order, including the ones with no tiers, as an explicit 'no tiers' entry rather than skipping them. The positional pairing then stays aligned, and the untameable seeds are recorded as what they are instead of being omitted.
untameable_creatures.analytical_value_of_a_no_tier_scan: Not zero, but close. It says nothing about the seed->tier function, since the creature has no tier. It is worth recording only so the pairing stays aligned and so the labelable subset of the 497 untamed seeds can be estimated - the practical sample size for the reopened search is smaller than 497 by however many scanned creatures are flying, swimming or otherwise untameable, and that fraction is not yet known.
untameable_creatures.open_question: Whether a creature's record itself reveals tameability - if it does, the untameable seeds could be filtered out of the save without the player having to look at each one. Not yet investigated; the Animal record's fields are a timestamp, the seeds, the system and the planet, so it may well not.
